method: Actual frozen game cores, current later mission wrappers, real published SFX manifest and independently controlled Web Audio/fetch/decode lifecycle mocks. No browser, real network, speech engine, MP3 codec or audio-quality claim.

results.name: Published recorded catalog, bounded asynchronous preload and shared context
All five actual scene shot paths use distinct recorded pools and rotate variants
Real deck HP hits and deaths deduplicate; callbacks and player state remain intact
Actual MRG bullets distinguish misses, nonlethal hits, and death; no vocal reaction on a miss
Real grenade keeps one explosion and distinct coalesced soldier deaths
Actual player HP damage in normal/calm space, deck and MRG; invulnerability prevents duplicates
MRG knife and late-loaded deck ninja use knife recordings; gunner uses gun recordings
Robodog deaths and actual Galaga drone kills never produce human voices
Actual space and convoy projectile kills coalesce legacy type-labelled destroy events into one mechanical death
Rare death lines are recorded, approximately 30%, spaced ≥6.5 s, one at a time and never queued
The real prepared captain immediately interrupts soldier speech and gets priority while loading/playing
Cold game events remain synchronous and never replay after asynchronous fetch/decode
Cancelled late fetch/body/decode, suspended resume and scene changes cannot start obsolete previews
Pause, mute, hidden page, exit and cleanup stop only effects while preserving music and the shared context
Voice and sample polyphony are bounded, completed nodes disconnect, radio cancels independently
HTTP/decode failures and absent Audio/fetch do not break actual gameplay or cause retry storms
Audio observation and previews preserve real gameplay state, seed and late replacement emit callback
